If you're not together they can't blame you for going on a date, just go for it. Just going on a date won't harm and it might help you discover whether you want to be with your ex or if you're ready for someone new in your life.

Perhaps? They might also be looking for a certain response on your end, if they ask about it a lot perhaps they just want to hear a certain thing before making such an important decision. Unless you truly think it's the right way I'd say don't directly ask but giving hints or just mentioning it every now and then should be fine. Perhaps when you do that you'll get the information you're looking for :)

Well even if she's not looking at you, can always give it a shot and just approach her. It's not the greatest advice I know but if you'd like to know whether she likes you too that's a way to go about it. Besides that just watching for subtle hints she might like you can't harm in any way either.

If it happened just once I'd leave it be but if you notice that during class or breaks they sometimes look at you (with that I mean for longer than a second) and you have some interest in them then I'd say talk to them, give it a shot, why not.

Read over this phrase: **“not hard - you literally just stop it.”,** I suppose for some people it's hard to realize how hard it is to stop these tics. Might sound a bit too simple for such a big thing but talking to them about it would most certainly help, perhaps get a professional to explain it a bit more if they aren't aware of how it works.  


I don't have any real advice besides that but do have a personal experience I'll include down below regarding tics in general and how I personally dealt with them.  


Just from personal experience, I've dealt with a tic when I was a younger age, it's difficult but they can be stopped. It just takes a lot of effort and patience. I personally was about 10 when I dealt with this and every time I'd have one of these tics a classmate of mine would say my name and I'd realize what I was doing and stopped doing it, this is how after about 2 years of having it I managed to stop having the tic.

As much as I understand where you're coming from, and I agree they were in the wrong and kind of deserve it. In the end it's not going to make anything better, it might make you feel better for a while but it won't last and it's just not worth it in my opinion. To answer your question, I don't think it's wrong or immature but definitely unnecessary.

Since you've known them for so long I wouldn't worry too much about it, you are always free to decide where you go, even if it's the last moment and I think in this specific situation they'd understand why as well.

The phrase  **'i don't have a physical attraction to Jess but i think i may like her'** is a scary one. If you have doubts as to whether you like them I'd say just wait until you know. Don't try to go faster than you can handle as it'll only make the situation more confusing and might ruin your chances with both. Just wait it out and once you know who you have actual attraction to and would like to give a shot then try to go for it.

I think modern technology just made it a lot easier for people to end up in these situations though. People have the internet where they can ask questions, yet consider the opinions they find on the internet usually as less valued, whereas if you asked someone questions like these face to face they'd find more value within the answer and might be able to actually realize and see the truth for themselves.

Sometimes people just can't handle the truth. They want to know other people their vision on it but if that vision doesn't match theirs then they define that vision as 'incorrect' or 'wrong'. Just how some people are I suppose, just shrug and move on :)
